# Method Endurance

> Chris Chatham's triathlon coaching business in Ballarat, Victoria, with online coaching for athletes anywhere. Formerly GPC Ballarat coaching. Each athlete's coach writes their program in TrainingPeaks and reads their week if they fill in the onboarding form and the weekly feedback app. Athletes can call or text their coach from 7am to 8pm.

## Coach
Chris Chatham: Victoria Triathlon Coach of the Year 2025, 2026 Standard Distance National Age Group Champion, 9x Ironman finisher, 11x Ironman 70.3 finishes, 6x World Championships qualifier. Australian Triathlon Development Coach (Triathlon Australia), TrainingPeaks Level 2.

## Packages (per week, GST included; no joining fee, no minimum term, two weeks' notice)
- Remote+, $55: for remote and international athletes. A weekly program with a Basic TrainingPeaks account, the feedback app, regular check-ins, technique analysis by video, a race nutrition plan, zone testing every six months and coached race weekends at selected events each season. Remote athletes can choose any of the three.
- Performance, $70: everything in Remote+, plus extra analysis at each training block (cadence and zone reviews, swim analysis in person), a link to book bike fit and sweat testing (paid separately by the athlete), coached squad sessions in Ballarat, a goal-race nutrition plan, a racing calendar planned for the year and technique work. Most remote athletes choose this.
- Performance+, $100: everything in Performance, plus weekly analysis, a one-to-one check-in at least weekly, race plans and post-race analysis, zone testing as needed and TrainingPeaks Premium. A small number of athletes.
Squad sessions come with Performance and Performance+ only. They are in Ballarat (track on Wednesdays, runs on Tuesdays, a Sunday run at Lake Wendouree normally at 8am, swims at Lake Wendouree). Times change with weather and race blocks and are shared in the squad chat.

## How to start
The free assessment is a short online form: three questions, then how to reach you. Chris replies within 4 hours, between 7am and 8pm.

## Journal
- [Australian Alpine Ascent Xtreme Triathlon](https://www.methodendurance.com.au/journal/alpine-ascent): 21 of 42 starters did not finish. Both Method athletes finished, and one of them was me.
- [Re-framing Pre-Race Anxiety](https://www.methodendurance.com.au/journal/pre-race-anxiety): Tight chest, restless legs, a thousand what-ifs. Why that's normal, and how to make it useful.
- [Pretty Isn't Always Practical (But It Can Be)](https://www.methodendurance.com.au/journal/pretty-vs-practical): Matching kit is fun. Function still comes first.
- [Lessons from a Cairns DNF](https://www.methodendurance.com.au/journal/cairns-dnf): Seventh out of the water, then a saddle bolt sheared about 25 km into the bike.
- [Bike Spares – What to pack and how to carry](https://www.methodendurance.com.au/journal/bike-spares): What I carry on race day, and where it all goes on the bike.
- [Full Distance Ironman World Championships – Nice, France](https://www.methodendurance.com.au/journal/ironman-worlds-nice): The full-distance Worlds, from the Parade of Nations to the finish chute.
- [70.3 World Championships – Lahti, Finland](https://www.methodendurance.com.au/journal/703-worlds-lahti): Racing the Worlds more than 15,000 km from home, with a virus that turned up two nights before.
